text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- The interior ministry is to investigate Istanbul and Adapazari municipalities for providing coaches to an illegal Islamist protest in Ankara against secularist education plans.
- Two leading businessmen plan to invest in the impoverished southeast region after realising its poor state at a "poverty summit".
MILLIYET
- The Supreme Military Council meets on Friday to decide on senior appointments in the armed forces.
- The Istanbul Stock Exchange donates $200 million to support the government's secularist education plans.
HURRIYET
- The testimonies of policemen suspected in the killing of a leftist journalist show that the police force sees the media as an enemy.
- President Suleyman Demirel says trade and industry should all be handed over to the private sector in the next few years.
YENI YUZYIL
- Police are put on alert as Islamists are expected to hold protests against secularist education reforms after Moslem Friday prayers.
CUMHURIYET
- Former police chief Alaattin Yuksel says the possibility of becoming a policeman after only three to five months training is a weaknesses in the Turkish police force.
RADIKAL
- The trade minister says better taxation monitoring will raise tax revenues by 20 percent.
- A parliamentary commission approves a draft law suspending the prison sentences of legally responsible newspaper editors.
DUNYA
- State Minister Isin Celebi unveils a package to boost exports and reach a target of $50 billion exports in five years.
ZAMAN
- The Kurdistan Democratic Party, a leading northern Iraqi faction, denies that a rival group seeking self rule in southeast Turkey has taken control of parts of northern Iraq.
